Multi-Evidence Centrality

Source: R/centrality-batch65.R
centrality_multi_evidence.Rd

Multi-evidence centrality (MeC; Mo and Deng 2019) fuses four measures of a node with Dempster's rule of combination. For each measure \(X\), a node is given a degree of belief that it is important and one that it is not, $$m_X(h) = \frac{X_i - X_{min}}{X_{max} - X_{min} + \omega}, \qquad m_X(l) = \frac{X_{max} - X_i}{X_{max} - X_{min} + \omega},$$ and the rest is left undecided. The four assignments are combined, and the score is the combined belief in "important" minus that in "not important". The measures are degree, betweenness, efficiency and correlation centrality.

Usage

centrality_multi_evidence(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality. The measure uses evidence_omega (default 1) and coc_alpha (the distance exponent of correlation centrality, default 3).

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. Degree is divided by \(n - 1\), betweenness by the number of pairs of other nodes, and efficiency is the sum of reciprocal distances divided by \(n\); the fourth measure is centrality_correlation_centrality with its coc_alpha. The score lies between -1 and 1. evidence_omega is 1 by default, the value of the source's example; a smaller value leaves less belief undecided and can change the ranking, although the source says it does not. Nodes that cannot be reached add nothing to efficiency. The implementation reproduces the 21 values the source prints for the ARPA network to three decimals, on an edge list recovered from the other columns of the same table. An evidence_omega that is not above 0 and at most 1 raises a cograph_bad_parameter error. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Mo, H. and Deng, Y. (2019). Identifying node importance based on evidence theory in complex networks. Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications, 529, 121538. doi:10.1016/j.physa.2019.121538 .

See also

centrality_correlation_centrality, centrality_harmonic, centrality_betweenness, centrality.

Examples

centrality_multi_evidence(regulation_net)
#>     Explore        Plan     Monitor       Adapt     Reflect     Discuss 
#> -0.16583870  0.19407151  0.46352156  0.25217195 -0.09987659 -0.12320936 
#>  Synthesize    Evaluate      Create       Share 
#> -0.46590169 -0.13077413  0.16640845 -0.15980283
